newsitem.title: POLAND: Cargill buys fourth feed plant in Poland.
newsitem.headline: Cargill buys fourth feed plant in Poland.

text.p: U.S. food trading and processing company Cargill has extended its investment in Poland by buying the Ropczyce feed plant, in the southeast of the country, the company said on Friday.
It said in a statement it would invest $2.5 million over the next six months in Ropczyce, its fourth feed plant in Poland. It did not say how much it had paid for the company.

Cargill bought the plant from Przedsiebiorstwo Przemyslu Zbozowo-Mlynarskiego SA (PZZ SA), a firm controlled by the National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 11, an institution created under Poland's mass privatisation programme.

Cargill said it planned to produce feed for pigs, poultry and cattle in the plant and double its capacity to 100,000 tonnes annually. It said the plant's 52 workers would continue to receive wages for 12 months.
Last year, Cargill said it wanted to invest $20-40 million by the year 2000 in Poland, where it had already invested nearly $60 million.
